context: Panama-flagged crude tanker ceased AIS transmissions in the central Red Sea while transiting northbound toward the Suez Canal. Last known position places the vessel within the Houthi maritime interdiction corridor. No distress signal received. Vessel had not been linked to Israeli ownership; motive for dark transit unclear.

General cargo vessel disappeared near Bab-el-Mandeb and reappeared 330nm to the east off the Somali coast. The displacement is inconsistent with declared routing to the Suez Canal and suggests the vessel transited through the Gulf of Aden to a non-declared waypoint during the gap. UKMTO was not notified.

Liberian-flagged product tanker went dark off the Yemeni coast near Hodeida, a key Houthi-controlled port. Extended dark period with no reappearance. Vessel class and size are consistent with shadow-fleet crude lifting operations that have been documented in Houthi-held waters to move sanctioned Iranian origin product.

Greek-flagged cargo vessel had a 22-hour AIS gap in the Gulf of Aden. Reappeared approximately 87nm east of last known position. Displacement is broadly consistent with vessel speed of ~4 knots, suggesting reduced speed or stop rather than a significant diversion. Assessment: equipment malfunction or deliberate avoidance during Houthi threat period.

Unknown-flagged tanker with a history of irregular AIS patterns went dark in southern Red Sea. Vessel previously identified in AIS spoofing cluster near Iranian waters. Flag state could not be confirmed — vessel appears to have cycled through three flag states in 2024. Likely component of sanctioned-crude lifting operation.

Cyprus-flagged cargo vessel experienced a brief AIS outage near Djibouti port approaches. Reappearance 18nm from last known position, consistent with anchorage hold and transponder malfunction or administrative shutdown for port call procedures. Low operational significance.

Belize-flagged tanker of unknown cargo went dark in the central Red Sea and has not reappeared. Last known position is within the active Houthi anti-ship missile engagement zone. Vessel was traveling without escort. If vessel is intact, prolonged silence near Houthi-controlled waters is consistent with shadow fleet operations.

Bahamas-flagged cargo vessel went dark in the northern Red Sea and reappeared 198nm northwest — near the Eritrean/Sudanese maritime border. Displacement and direction are inconsistent with declared transit to Suez. Vessel possibly diverted to an unlisted port call. No cargo manifest deviation confirmed.

Very large crude carrier of unknown flag departed Kharg Island area and disappeared within the Strait of Hormuz transit corridor. AIS history shows repeated dark periods correlated with crude lifting operations from Iranian export terminals. Almost certainly operating as part of the IRGC-linked shadow fleet. US OFAC monitoring active.

Unknown-flagged tanker last observed stationary near Qeshm Island — a known anchorage for IRGC-linked vessels conducting ship-to-ship crude transfers. Extended AIS silence at this location is consistent with the operational pattern of Iranian sanctions evasion using falsified documentation and AIS spoofing.

Malta-flagged general cargo vessel went dark in the Persian Gulf and reappeared 223nm to the southeast near Muscat, Oman. The displacement suggests an unreported port call, possibly at a small Iranian coastal facility. Cargo manifest covered general goods; inspection at Muscat confirmed non-hazardous cargo but 48-hour berthing unaccounted for.

Singapore-flagged product tanker went dark for 48 hours in the Gulf of Oman. Reappearance close to last known position with limited displacement suggests the vessel was stationary or near-stationary during the gap. Assessed as likely technical fault or deliberate shutdown during a scheduled maintenance window. Low operational concern.

Cameroon-flagged cargo vessel went dark in Iranian coastal waters northeast of the Strait of Hormuz near Bandar Abbas. The vessel's last port of call was a minor Iranian port not commonly used by legitimate commercial traffic. Dark transit in Iranian-controlled waters is consistent with contraband or weapons component movement.

Turkish-flagged tanker transiting from the Gulf of Oman toward the Strait of Hormuz experienced a 24-hour AIS outage. Reappearance position is consistent with continued slow progress on the same route. Low displacement and short duration assessed as AIS equipment failure. No suspicious activity pattern.

Chinese-flagged fishing vessel ceased AIS transmissions in the disputed Spratly Islands area. Vessel was observed stationary for 72 hours before going dark — a pattern consistent with Chinese maritime militia 'presence operations' used to assert de facto control over contested features. Fishing vessel designation likely covers maritime militia role.

Unknown-flagged cargo vessel disappeared near the Chinese-administered Paracel Islands. AIS history shows irregular patterns consistent with vessels that regularly transit between mainland Chinese ports and island outposts without following standard commercial routing. Assessed as possible PLA resupply mission or sensitive cargo transit.

Philippine-flagged fishing vessel went dark in the vicinity of Second Thomas Shoal, a contested feature where Philippine forces maintain a deliberate grounding. Reappearance 391nm to the northeast near Palawan is geographically anomalous for a fishing boat. Possible coerced departure or displacement from patrol during China Coast Guard standoff.

Vietnamese-flagged tanker went dark in Vietnamese EEZ waters south of Da Nang. Location is within an area where Chinese survey vessels have operated. No hostile activity reported. Assessed as moderate concern — dark transit in a contested EEZ reduces maritime domain awareness and may indicate Vietnamese vessel seeking to avoid surveillance.

Unknown vessel type and flag, last seen in the central South China Sea, reappeared in Chinese coastal waters near Zhanjiang — home of the PLA Southern Theater Naval Command. A 567nm displacement over 5 days at average 4.5 knots, combined with complete flag obfuscation, is strongly indicative of a PLA intelligence-gathering or survey vessel conducting deliberate AIS-off operations.

Hong Kong-flagged cargo vessel went dark in the Taiwan Strait the day before the PLA's Joint Sword-2024A exercise encirclement drill. Timing raises concern that the vessel may have received advance warning of the exercise closure zones and deliberately disabled AIS to transit without logging a record of crossing disputed sea areas.

Taiwan-flagged tanker went dark during a period of elevated PLA Rocket Force activity in the Taiwan Strait. Reappearance 93nm to the south on a consistent transit heading. Assessed as deliberate AIS shutdown to reduce identification risk during perceived high-threat period, consistent with ROC commercial vessel risk-mitigation guidance.

Marshall Islands-flagged cargo vessel went dark in the Luzon Strait — the deep-water passage between the Philippines and Taiwan used by PLA submarines transiting to the Pacific. Extended dark period near this strategically sensitive waterway, combined with vessel's recent history of unusual track deviations, elevates concern about cargo nature or undisclosed port calls.

Malta-flagged tanker went dark in waters south of Cyprus, in close proximity to the SEA-ME-WE 5 undersea cable system landing at Limassol. Extended dark period near critical communications infrastructure without plausible commercial routing explanation. Pattern is broadly consistent with vessel conducting slow-speed survey near cable routes — a concern flagged by NATO infrastructure protection programs.

Liberian-flagged cargo vessel went dark near the Lebanese EEZ and reappeared 162nm northwest near the coast of Cyprus. Partial displacement pattern is broadly consistent with an unreported port call in the Lebanese or Syrian coastal zone — areas subject to sanctions monitoring for weapons and dual-use goods transit.

Togo-flagged tanker went dark near the Lebanese coast. Togo is a commonly used flag of convenience for vessels linked to Iranian oil export operations and sanctions evasion networks. Location near Beirut port approaches, which has been used historically to receive Iranian fuel shipments to Hezbollah-affiliated entities, elevates the intelligence significance.
